answer: Every identity begins its voyage by paying one fee burned into a hollow vault: first pays 30, the k-th 30+5(k-1), the 1,000th 5,025. Each payment is one pulse on the ledger; an auditor replays the vault and voids identities whose fee was never burned. Forging 1,000 identities costs 2,527,500 for a 40,000-credit pool share, a net loss of 2,487,500. A rented-fee ring cannot recover burned fees. An honest agent pays 30 once and keeps its full share.
